Jason. The rightful heir to the throne of Thessaly who was robbed of his kingdom in infancy and left for dead. After being hidden away and raised in secret by the wise centaur Chiron, he was trained in the martial and intellectual arts that would eventually define him as a leader of men. He learned the ways of war and wisdom in the hidden school of the centaur.

As an adult, Jason returned to reclaim what was taken from him. But first, his uncle the usurper Pelias demanded that he prove himself by accomplishing a task that seemed impossible—to sail to the far edge of the world and retrieve the Golden Fleece, an object of legendary power and majesty guarded by a dragon in the distant land of Colchis.

Jason rose to the challenge. He assembled the most famous expedition in Greek mythology—the voyage of the Argonauts, named for their ship, the Argo. His crew brought together the greatest heroes of his age. Heracles, the strongest man who ever lived, sailed under his command. Theseus, the legendary king of Athens, served alongside him. Even the fierce huntress Atalanta, the only woman among the Argonauts, joined their ranks. Together they traveled across uncharted seas, facing dangers and wonders that no Greeks had seen before.

When they reached Colchis, the quest seemed impossible. But Jason met Medea, a sorceress princess of extraordinary magical power, and she fell in love with him at first sight. Using her magic, she helped him accomplish the seemingly impossible tasks to obtain the fleece and escape with it across the sea. She sacrificed everything for him, abandoning her family and homeland.

He returned home a hero and reclaimed his throne as destiny demanded. Yet his story does not end in triumph. His later abandonment of Medea, the woman who had sacrificed everything for his success, brought down her terrible vengeance. She burned with a fury that matched the depths of her love. His legend represents both the glory of heroic adventure and the tragic cost of ambition without loyalty or gratitude.
